links.outcome: Culturally appropriate LLM responses to health questions from personas signaling cultural norms
links.effect: Even the best of five models gave culturally appropriate responses only 20-30% of the time. Afghan context averaged 8.8%. Explicit cultural-cue (CoT) prompting improved results by only 3-5% on average.
links.quote: Benchmarking five leading models reveals that even the best achieve culturally appropriate responses only 20-30% of the time.

unlisted_practices: Chain-of-thought prompting that directs the model to attend to cultural cues in conversation history
Evaluating cultural competence as implicitly signaled norm adherence rather than static demographic traits

screen.reason: Evaluates LLM cultural competence and safety across diverse cultural personas asking health questions, and tests the effect of explicitly prompting the model to focus on culturally relevant cues (prompt guardrail/strategy).
